intelligence.human_view: A footer that was never finished is a promise the page makes and does not keep: "Finished Means Working" says the work is done — and the footer itself is the proof that it is not. The rating is the intelligence rating itself: LOVE / LIKE / SHARE, VALUE and INTELLIGENCE scored in stars, and then MAKE THIS INTELLIGENCE BETTER — Add Evidence, Build On This, Ask A Question, Report An Outcome, Contribute Intelligence. That is the loop closing on every post: the reader rates what they read, and the rating makes the intelligence better. Unfinished, the loop never closes — the intelligence is served but never scored, never built on, never reported back. And "I hadn't mentioned it in a long time" is itself the lesson: a thing unmentioned is a thing forgotten — the loop's job is to remember it, so the footer is not forgotten again. The color ruling is still owed (VALUE gold + INTELLIGENCE blue, his pick, 9/10) — a ruling owed is a ruling recorded, not a ruling made.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build a beautiful tower, and right at the bottom there's a little sign that says "Finished Means Working!" — but the sign was never finished! That's silly, right? And the sign is supposed to let everyone say whether they LOVE it or LIKE it, and give it stars — 9 out of 10 for how useful it is, 10 out of 10 for how smart it is — and then tell you how to make it even better! Shawn says: don't forget the sign. Finish it!
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says the little rating footer at the bottom of the Hub was never finished, dear — and he hadn't mentioned it in ever so long. It says "Finished Means Working", dear — LOVE, LIKE, SHARE — and you rate the intelligence with stars, 9 out of 10 for value and 10 out of 10 for intelligence. And then you can make it better, dear — add evidence, build on it, ask a question, report what happened, contribute your own intelligence. It's a lovely thing, dear — it just needs finishing.
